item.title: Brewers Rival Reportedly 'Interested' In Stealing Key Reliever In Free Agency
item.description: Free agent pitcher JoJo Romero The Milwaukee Brewers won the World Series, and some key players from their championship team are now free agents. One of the key players on the open market now is JoJo Romero, whom the Brewers acquired at the trade deadline from the St. Louis Cardinals. Romero was a key part of the Brewers' dominant bullpen in October, and according to The St. Louis Post-Dispatch's Derrick Goold reported that the Cardinals are interested in a reunion. "According to sources familiar with the team’s view of this offseason, they would like to discuss Romero’s return just months after the team traded him to the Brewers," wrote Goold. Romero was on the injured list when the Brewers got him and was recovering from an appendectomy. He pitched in 11 regular-season games with the Brewers, posting a 3.38 ERA. In the postseason, he posted a 1.13 ERA in seven games, working eight total innings. The only run he gave up was a solo home run in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. It was his first time pitching in the postseason, and he proved his value as part of a team looking to win a championship. He earned himself some money with his postseason performance, and the Cardinals could use him back. The Cardinals have some talented players and could be competing for a postseason spot next year. Getting Romero back in the bullpen could help them secure one of the wild card spots. More MLB: Dodgers' Blake Snell Comments On Tarik Skubal's Free Agency

item.title: Joe Mazzulla on Kristaps Porzingis stepping away from the NBA
item.description: In the wake of the news of former Boston Celtics big man Kristaps Porzingis electing to step away from the game in light of the lingering health issues the Latvian big man has dealt with since his tenure with the Celtics, Boston head coach Joe Mazzulla revealed he reached out to his former center. "I talked to him on the plane," said Mazzulla via CLNS Media. "I reached out to him I think (I) had a good conversation with him." "Also, some other guys on the staff did as well," he added. "I think it's just a good reminder, as you know, we go through the NBA season and look at these guys as athletes and look at them as basketball players. They're a lot more than that, and so I think that is a good reminder of that. And their platform, their life, their careers are so much more than what happens on the court there, so It's a good reminder of that." "We're able to talk to him about it," added the Celtics coach. "But he's in a pretty good space and whatever we can do to help him, we will. We're grateful for the time that I got to spend with him, on and off the court." "A guy when he comes into the room he lights the room up, lights the locker room up," said Mazzulla. "I thought the years he was there he was like the icebreaker." "He brought a sense of joy to the rigors of the season and playing for the Celtics, and he brought a joy to that. I think he had a positive impact on the locker room." item.description: GLENDALE, AZ: Welbyn Francisca of the Cleveland Guardians bats for the Surprise Saguaros against the Glendale Desert Dogs in a 2026 Arizona Fall League game at Camelback Ranch on Oct. 15, 2026. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) Getty Images Watch shortstop Welbyn Francisca at bat in a Cleveland Guardians uniform hit from either side of the plate and you immediately think of Francisco Lindor. Before the 2026 Arizona Fall League Fall Stars game, I asked the 20-year-old prospect who his favorite player was as a boy growing up in the Dominican Republic. “Francisco Lindor,” he said. Daniel Robertson, his manager this fall with the Surprise Saguaros, said, “Yeah, you see that. But … I think he’s more Roberto Alomar.” Whoa! Alomar is considered by many the best all-around second baseman in history. His Hall of Fame plaque in Cooperstown, NY tells it all. COOPERSTOWN, NY: The National Baseball Hall of Fame plaque of Roberto Alomar. CHUCK MURR / Forbes.com Cleveland fans enjoyed Alomar’s play for the final three (1999-2001) of his 12 consecutive All-Star seasons. It was the finest stretch of his career, as Alomar averaged 21 homers, 38 doubles, 103 RBI, 122 runs and 35 stolen bases while playing stellar, Gold Glove defense. Cleveland management has tried to get as many Alomar-type infielders as possible ever since. The parade of switch-hitters wearing a Cleveland uniform in an MLB All-Star game since includes Omar Vizquel, Asdrubal Cabrera, Victor Martinez, Carlos Santana, Lindor, and Jose Ramirez, who is on his way to breaking most of the franchise’s offensive records. Young switch-hitters Bryan Rocchio, Angel Martinez and Angel Genao have begun making their marks the past couple seasons. Robertson says make way for Francisca. “There is a smoothness to his game where like no moment is too big for him, ever,” said Robertson, now the Triple-A Columbus (OH) Clippers’ bench coach who played briefly for four MLB teams including Cleveland a decade ago. "I think the longevity piece will be at second base. I think he can play short as long as he wants to, but I think that if you just put him at second and stick him in the No. 2 or 3 hole and just let him hit for 15 years it’s going to be special. "Then you just go coach the guys that need pushing. “I don’t know if he has it all figured out yet, but he’s just a baby at 20. He has the mindset, the moxie, to take the lessons that the game itself gives you, adjust and move forward.” Francisca’s Approach In only 16 games this fall, Francisca leads the AFL in multiple categories: 31 hits, .417 average, 28 RBI, 53 total bases, .716 slugging percentage, and 1,199 OPS. He went 5-for-5 with a double, homer, three runs and three RBI on October 3. “Just having fun and trying to learn every day,” he said. item.title: Joe Root to lead England in South Africa Tests; Shoaib Bashir and Ollie Pope left out
item.description: England have announced a 15-member squad for their three-match Test series against South Africa, which will be part of the 2025-27 World Test Championship (WTC). Joe Root will captain the side, while Liam Patterson-White has received his maiden Test call-up following an impressive County Championship season in 2026. Patterson-White was the most successful spinner in the competition, earning him a place in the squad. Jacob Bethell has also returned after recovering from a knee injury. However, spinner Shoaib Bashir and batter Ollie Pope have been left out. Dan Lawrence makes a comeback as an additional batting option who can also contribute with the ball. New faces and changes in England's squad England's pace attack includes Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Ollie Robinson, Sam Cook and Sonny Baker. Explaining the selection, national selector Marcus North said the team was prepared for a tough challenge against the reigning World Test champions. “We have selected a strong and balanced squad that is ready for the challenge of facing a South African team that are ICC Test World Champions and who returned to the top of the ICC Test rankings following their recent 2-1 series win over Australia,” North said. He also confirmed two changes from the squad that defeated Pakistan 3-0 in the home summer series, with Patterson-White earning his first call-up and Bethell returning from injury. WTC standings and series schedule England are currently sixth in the WTC 2025-27 standings with 38.64 percentage points, while South Africa are second with 71.43 per cent. The series will begin in Johannesburg from December 17 to 21. The second Test will be played in Centurion from December 26 to 30, while the final match is scheduled in Cape Town from January 3 to 7. The tour will follow England's limited-overs series in Australia. item.title: Cowboys ‘wise move’ with George Pickens amid trade rumors might be unpopular
item.description: Cowboys ‘wise move’ with George Pickens amid trade rumors might be unpopular originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys , following their Week 9 win over the Indianapolis Colts , are 4-5 in the regular season. They're sitting right behind the 5-2-1 New York Giants in the NFC East, and there's still a very real chance they go on a playoff run. But, for the 2026 NFL trade deadline, the Cowboys could go any sort of direction. They could buy, or they could even consider trading away key players. One player who's emerged as a trade candidate is wide receiver George Pickens. ESPN NFL insider Dan Graziano revealed what the "wise move" would be with Pickens, and it's one that might not be popular among Cowboys fans. NFL insider reveals 'wise move' Cowboys can make with George Pickens "The wise move for Dallas would be to see what teams would be willing to five up for Pickens," Graziano writes. "Maybe that's how they find the help they need on defense -- some kind of player-for-player swap with a team desperate for wide receiver help." If the Cowboys do listen to trade offers for Pickens leading up to the NFL trade deadline on November 10, then they surely could get some strong offers for desperate teams. One such team could be the Kansas City Chiefs . Add in teams like the New England Patriots , San Francisco 49ers , Pittsburgh Steelers , Los Angeles Rams , and maybe even the Seattle Seahawks , and the Cowboys could probably get a strong return for Pickens. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade Graziano believes it would be the "wise move" for the Cowboys to listen to offers for Pickens, even though their Week 9 win has them within striking distance of the NFC East title. It might be unpopular, but Dallas should really listen to offers for Pickens. CeeDee Lamb is great as a No. 1 option, and Ryan Flournoy has shown enough to be an intriguing secondary receiver. Even if the Cowboys only get draft compensation for Pickens, after their trade for Joey Porter Jr., some extra capital over the next draft or two wouldn't hurt. With Pickens set to hit free agency after this season, offers for the veteran WR should be something this Cowboys team is willing to listen to. The only question might be if Jerry Jones is willing to do this "wise move" and, at the very least, listen to offers. item.description: When the College Football Playoff title game was in Houston in 2024, it was a four-team field. It is expanding to 24 teams, starting in the 2027 season. A look at what we know so far: The field The 24-team field will be comprised of the four conference champions from the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC (as determined by their respective conferences), the highest-ranked team from the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12, or Sun Belt; and the 19 highest-ranked remaining teams in the final CFP selection committee ranking. item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Oilers coach Mike Babcock explains Jake Walman scratch vs. Rangers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Edmonton Oilers are off to a terrific start in 2026-27, winning 12 times in 18 tries and leading the Pacific Division in the early going. The same can’t be said for Jake Walman, who has managed just one assist in 11 contests, along with a minus-eight rating. He’s set to be a healthy scratch for the fifth time in the last seven games when the Oilers welcome the New York Rangers to Rogers Place on Monday night. Head coach Mike Babcock explained the decision after the team’s morning skate. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I just think the bottom line is: what do you do without the puck? What chances are you involved in? What do you do when you have it?” Babcock told reporters, including Daily Faceoff Edmonton’s Michael Menzies. “And it’s a hard, hard league, and so each and every night, we evaluate the whole situation, and unlike you guys who watch it once, we watch it over and over again with five people, and so we got a pretty good handle on the thing. “Then, lots of times, the analytics from the outside aren’t what we have on the inside, and so what we do is we just try to make the best decisions to help the team be successful. item.title: He replaced a Connecticut baseball legend. Then Dave Werkhoven built a legacy of his own
item.description: Former Shepaug baseball coach Dave Werkhoven, left, with longtime Spartans scorekeeper Ray Reich. (Courtesy of the Werkhoven family) WASHINGTON, Conn. - It's a truism in sports that you don't want to be the coach who replaces a legend. Yet Dave Werkhoven not only replaced the man who built the Shepaug baseball program, he became an icon in the community in his own right. And he began creating his own legacy under the most trying of circumstances. When Werkhoven had to take the helm of the Spartans late in the 1984 season, it was immediately following the death from cancer of Ted Alex, his mentor, neighbor, best friend and the man whose name already adorned the storybook ballpark in Washington Depot. "Coach Werkhoven had big shoes to fill and he more than did that," said Mike Kersten, a catcher on Werkhoven's early teams and a Shepaug assistant coach for many years. "He carried the torch of Coach Alex, and he made his own history." Werkhoven died of a stroke Tuesday, Nov. 3. He was 80. In one regard, Werkhoven even outdid Alex, winning three Class S state championships to Alex's two. Like Alex, he won more than 300 victories in his 20 years as head coach, finishing with a record of 342-103 to go with nine Berkshire League titles. "When Mr. Alex passed, it had to be a challenge to pick it up and carry it forward," said Scott Werkhoven, who succeeded his father as head coach in 2005. "But it was always about this is the way Ted did it and this is how we're going to keep doing it." A native of Ellington, Werkhoven arrived at Shepaug in 1970 with his new wife, Susan, to teach chemistry and biology. They expected to stay only a year or two, but instead spent a lifetime. Alex enlisted Werkhoven as an assistant coach at their first meeting. He also lined up the young couple with the house across the street from his, which was a strategic decision in more ways than one: The Werkhovens became convenient baby-sitters for Alex and his wife Ruth's five children. In their 15 seasons together, Shepaug won state titles in 1973 and '83. After Alex, who finished with 385 victories and 16 BL titles in 28 seasons, died on the eve of the 1984 state tournament, Werkhoven, assisted by Gerry Carbone, ran the team in the postseason. He took over as head coach the following spring. "The first three or four years, I'm sure he felt enormous pressure," said Gary Alex, Ted's son. "He would joke himself, ‘Well, I may have screwed that one up.' But you're not an assistant for 15 years without learning something." Werkhoven not only taught the same brand of baseball, but the same code of conduct. "He was an extension of Coach Alex, not only in winning, but in doing things the right way. You wear your uniform correctly; you take the field the right way. You win with humility; you lose with grace," Kersten said. "He had a quiet intensity. He would dispute a call, but he never crossed the line. I don't recall him ever swearing or using profanity." Shepaug won its first state title

item.title: Noah Gragson Owes Daniel Suarez An Apology After Homestead Spin
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images During the final laps of the NASCAR Cup Series season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway, Noah Gragson spun Daniel Suarez. The contact happened on Lap 254 of 267 during a hard battle for 11th place. Gragson admitted he made the mistake. He did not try to hide the error or blame the track. He told the other driver he was wrong and meant it. The radio chatter before the crash made it look like the move was intentional. Gragson complained about Suarez blocking his air with 20 laps left. Insults flew over the airwaves. But the driver who caused the crash owned up to it right after the race. The two men shook hands. Gragson said the contact was not what he wanted. He just wanted to win the spot. A Full Admission of Guilt Gragson did not make excuses for hitting the left rear of Suarez’s car. He stood in front of the media and took the blame. He explained that he drove down to the bottom of the track and crossed a seam. The car got loose. He tried to save it but failed. He never wanted to spin out a competitor. The apology was clear and direct. The incident actually helped both drivers in the end. A caution flag came out after the crash. This allowed the field to bunch up. Suarez drove up to eighth place on the restart. Gragson finished ninth. They both ended up with a double top-ten finish. In the closing laps, Suarez passed Gragson without encountering any further trouble. Strong Finish for Gragson Despite the spin, Gragson finished higher than he had all season. He matched his best result of the year. Suarez secured 13th place in the final championship standings, beating absent teammate Carson Hocevar thanks to the race. Gragson felt good about the weekend despite a rough practice and qualifying session. He called Homestead one of his favorite racetracks. He noted that running the fence is fun. His car had a hole in the right-rear quarterpanel because he ran it into the wall for most of the race. “It’s probably my best racetrack and I feel like this is a place where we can at least contend and be competitive,” Gragson said, according to Motorsport.com . Grateful for a top 10 finish, he enters the offseason carrying momentum. The 2026 season ended on Sunday, November 8, 2026.

item.title: Sergio Garcia Targets 2027 Ryder Cup Spot After LIV Exit
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Sergio Garcia is pushing to return to the Ryder Cup after quitting LIV Golf. The 46-year-old Spaniard spoke with European captain Luke Donald about making the 2027 team. Garcia wants to play or help in any way he can at Adare Manor. DP World Tour rules could prevent him from leading the squad. He has the backing of Justin Rose but needs to clear a major hurdle to get back on the team. Garcia announced his departure from the rebel league just before new investor BC Partners pulled out of the deal. Garcia’s departure from the rebel league puts him back in the mix for European golf, though the path is narrow. He told Golf Magic he loves the competition and wants to be part of it again. The timing of his exit aligns with a push to join the DP World Tour ahead of the next big event. A Direct Line to the Captain Garcia has already reached out to the man in charge. He confirmed a conversation with Luke Donald took place in Ireland. During that talk, Garcia said he was trying his hardest to earn a spot. Donald responded by saying he did not expect anything else from the veteran player. This exchange gives Garcia a clear sign that the captain is open to his involvement. Garcia said he told Donald directly about his effort to make the team. The captain’s reply was supportive and straightforward. Garcia told Golf Magic, “I had a little chat with Luke in Ireland, mentioning that I was trying as hard as I could to make the team, and he said that he didn’t expect anything else, so that was nice.” This support is crucial for a player trying to re-enter the fold after years away. item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Dianna Russini is set to unveil her return to broadcasting with a new show and new column. Earlier this year, allegations of an affair between New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel and journalist Dianna Russini went viral. While Vrabel has continued in his role with the Patriots, Russini resigned from her role with The Athletic. Now after six months away from the spotlight, midway through the 2026 NFL season, Dianna Russini is making a return. item.description: Crystal Palace make Pierre Sage sack decision after Liverpool defeat Crystal Palace set for Pierre Sage exit as Thomas Frank leads Palace manager search Crystal Palace are expected to make a managerial change after the 3-1 defeat to Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League table, with Standard Sport reporting that Pierre Sage is now heading for the exit. The decision has appeared to be building for some time. Palace had already weighed up a change as early as September, only to hold back while assessing alternatives and monitoring whether defensive improvements could take hold. A goalless draw away to Leeds before the last international break offered some encouragement, but the wider trend has remained deeply concerning. After only two wins from his opening 10 league matches, the sense inside the club was that action was becoming unavoidable. Standard Sport states that Sage’s departure “has been mooted for some time”, and the expectation now is that Palace will “part ways with the Frenchman heading into the international break”. Palace defensive issues shaped outcome The context matters. Palace have not adequately replaced major departures, with Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi specifically highlighted. Even so, results and performances have left little room for patience. The report says Sage “struggled to get his ideas across”, while his “fixation with getting Palace to run and press ultimately caused frustration” as defensive weaknesses kept surfacing. Photo IMAGO That point is underlined by a grim statistic, Palace have conceded more goals than anyone else in the Premier League this season. There was also reportedly a feeling that Sage “was willing to die by his ideas”, a line that captures the rigidity Palace’s decision-makers appear to have seen. Key moments that increased pressure Several incidents are said to have heightened concern, among them the 5-0 defeat to Brighton and Sage’s call to drop Jaydee Canvot before the 3-2 loss to Ipswich. The report adds that “his lack of communication did not go down well with some players”, and that “even in victory, Palace were at times fortunate as their performances lacked control”. Succeeding Oliver Glasner “was always going to be a hard task”, but Palace now look ready to move on quickly, with Thomas Frank reportedly the leading candidate. item.title: 2026 CIAC girls soccer tournament first round is complete. What you need to know
item.description: Callie Fagan, center, of Darien fights for the ball with Grace Seltenreich, left, and Cecilia Schimenti, right, of Trumbull in Darien on October 8, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) The first round of the CIAC girls soccer tournaments was held Friday and Saturday. Here is the full schedule and scoreboard for the tournaments. Here is what you need to know. Seedings hold to form The new tournament format, which factors in strength of schedule, seems to have kept seeded upsets relatively rare so far. Previously, it was just winning percentage that was used to seed the four divisions. In Class L, all 10 first-round games were won by the higher seed. In Class S, 10 of the 11 higher seeds prevailed, and the one seeded upset was a 17 beating a 16. There were three seeded upsets in Class LL: No. 21 New Canaan over No. 12 Conard, No. 19 South Windsor over No. 14 Darien and No. 18 Fairfield Warde over No. 15 Fairfield Ludlowe. Seven of the nine higher-seeded teams in Class M advanced. No. 18 Plainville eliminated No. 15 Woodland and No. 17 Lakeview beat No. 16 Nonnewaug. This system is designed to reward teams for playing a difficult schedule. For example, Darien came in with a 7-8-1 record, but had the No. 14 seed in LL, instead of being 23rd. In the end, the Blue Wave were one of the seeded upsets in the first round. Lacrosse went to a similar power points system a few years back, with the better teams getting lower-numbered seeds and two of the top three or four seeds having a better opportunity to reach the state final. You can dominate a game in soccer, run into a hot goalkeeper and lose 1-0. So we shall see how many higher-seeded teams reach the semifinals. Goalkeeper sportsmanship A number of CIAC tournament games will be decided by penalty kicks. Maybe even in the state finals. The battle for Fairfield supremacy came down to penalty kicks on Friday between Ludlowe and Warde. The two goalkeepers, Warde's Cece Meyers, a senior, and Ludlowe's Jules Conrad, a junior, were able to get through both regulation and overtime without allowing a goal. Warde coach Kim Rasmussen noted the sportsmanship between the two goalkeepers - both of whom she coached at the youth level - through the PK session. "After making big saves, the two goalkeepers exchanged high fives, celebrating and acknowledging each other's efforts," Rasmussen said in an email. That quality could become particularly important during the demanding months ahead, when injuries, fatigue and difficult fixtures can affect every club. There is also an argument that Arsenal are better placed than many of their rivals to maintain consistency. Other teams may improve and put together winning runs, but Arteta’s side have already demonstrated that they can collect points regularly under different circumstances. The remaining 28 matches will undoubtedly bring challenges, and Arsenal are unlikely to avoid every setback. However, their current performances provide a strong foundation from which to approach the rest of the campaign. Every contender has the opportunity to improve, but every team will also experience difficult periods and unexpected defeats. item.title: Kansas suffers critical injury ahead of Kentucky matchup in Champions Classic
item.description: Kentucky Basketball has been battling the injury bug since back in the summer practice season. Thankfully, the Wildcats are getting healthy as regular-season play heats up, especially with Kam Williams making his return last week. The same cannot be said for the Kansas Jayhawks , who Kentucky will face in Tuesday’s Championship Classic without one of their most important players. On Monday, Kansas announced that sixth-year senior Melvin Council Jr. suffered a broken foot and will be out indefinitely. The school is hopeful that the 6-foot-4, 180-pound Council will return around the start of conference play, but for now, the standout guard will be out for the foreseeable future. That’s a massive loss for the Jayhawks, as Council is the team’s top point guard and easily one of their best players. Last season, he averaged 12.7 points, 5.1 assists, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.0 steals per game. Through two games this year, he’s averaged 8.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.5 rebounds, and 2.5 steals in 21 minutes per game. The class of 2021 high school prospect is currently eligible thanks to a court injunction. Without Council, Kansas will rely on true freshman Taylor Kinney, a native of Kentucky, and sophomore Leroy Blyden, a transfer from Toledo who Kentucky showed interest in this past offseason . Council infamously said he was considering Kentucky prior to making his commitment on October 4. As it turned out, Kentucky, nor anyone on Council’s list, was even recruiting him, as his return to Kansas had already been a done deal, and he was simply trolling other schools.
